title: Creamy Garlic Chicken Thigh, Mushroom & Spinach Skillet
description: One-pan chicken thighs in a garlicky mushroom sauce, made creamy with blended chickpeas instead of heavy cream. About 10g saturated fat for the whole pan.

ingredients.name: extra virgin olive oil, for searing
extra virgin olive oil, for vegetables
canned chickpeas, drained and rinsed (about half a can)
extra virgin olive oil, for finishing

instructions.text: Make the chickpea cream: Blend {10} chickpeas with 1/2 cup of the {9} chicken stock, {11} white miso, and {12} lemon juice until completely smooth, 60 to 90 seconds in a high-speed blender. Set aside. Keep the remaining 1/2 cup stock for the pan.

Season and sear the chicken: Pat {0} chicken thighs dry and season with {1} kosher salt and {2} black pepper (hold back a pinch of salt for the vegetables). Heat {3} olive oil in the Le Creuset on induction level 6. Sear the thighs 5 minutes per side until golden. They don't need to be cooked through. Move to a plate.

Cook onion and mushrooms: Drop to level 5. Add {4} olive oil, then {5} yellow onion with a pinch of salt. Cook until translucent, 2 to 3 minutes. Add {6} cremini mushrooms and cook until softened and browned, 4 to 5 minutes. Don't stir constantly; let them sit to brown.
Garlic and tomato paste: Stir in {7} garlic cloves and {8} tomato paste. Cook 1 minute, stirring, until the paste darkens slightly.

Deglaze and simmer the chicken: Pour in the reserved 1/2 cup stock and scrape up the browned bits. Return the chicken and any resting juices, nestling the thighs into the pan. Bring to a gentle bubble, then hold at level 4. Simmer partially covered 10 to 12 minutes, until the thighs reach 165°F. The liquid will reduce; that's fine.

Add the chickpea cream: Drop to level 2 to 3. Stir the chickpea cream into the pan around the chicken until smooth and heated through, about 1 minute. If it's thicker than you want, loosen with a splash of stock or water.

Wilt the spinach and finish: Stir in {13} baby spinach in handfuls until wilted, about 2 minutes. Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Drizzle with {14} olive oil just before serving for a silkier finish. Serve immediately; the sauce keeps thickening as it sits.

notes:
Portions: Dave ~57%, Jen ~43%. Dave's share is roughly 80g protein and ~6g saturated fat.

Serve over farro, quinoa, or whole wheat pasta to round it out.

Leftovers: the sauce tightens in the fridge, so reheat with a splash of stock. Good lunch candidate since it reheats well.
